questions.question: What happens when a binding price ceiling is below equilibrium?
questions.referenceAnswer: A shortage occurs because quantity demanded exceeds quantity supplied.

questions.question: What benefit is sacrificed when scarce resources are committed to one policy?
questions.referenceAnswer: The sacrificed benefit is the best alternative forgone—the policy's opportunity cost.

questions.question: Why does the side that changes its behavior less carry more of a tax burden?
questions.referenceAnswer: The less elastic side adjusts quantity less when the tax changes prices, so it bears more of the burden.

questions.question: What do economists call the road not taken when choosing?
questions.referenceAnswer: The road not taken is the opportunity cost: the best alternative forgone.

questions.question: How could rising demand contribute to inflation, and how might monetary policy respond?
questions.referenceAnswer: Demand growth can contribute to demand-pull inflation; a central bank may raise its policy rate to moderate aggregate demand.

questions.question: Does monetary policy take effect immediately?
questions.referenceAnswer: No. The notes say monetary policy operates with variable time lags.

questions.question: On what date is the final exam?
questions.referenceAnswer: The selected materials do not specify a final-exam date.

questions.question: Do the notes claim that one product becoming more expensive is always inflation?
expectedText: not merely an increase in one product's price
questions.referenceAnswer: No. Inflation is a sustained increase in the general price level, not one isolated price increase.

questions.question: What factors make demand less elastic?
questions.referenceAnswer: Demand tends to be less elastic when close substitutes are unavailable or buyers have little time to adjust.
